title: AID self-assembly and multistranded DNA binding drive synapsis in class switch recombination.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Retrieved the full open-access text and read the data availability statement and methods. Tried three routes to the data: the Europe PMC supplementary-file listing (timed out, one attempt at 120 s), the NCBI PMC open-access package service (HTTP 404, no package exists), and a text-wide scan for any repository accession (none found anywhere in the article, and Europe PMC's text-mining flags hasDbCrossReferences=N and hasTMAccessionNumbers=N). So I opened no data file.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about what the data contains. The paper states the raw single-molecule videos are 'available on request'; the supplementary tables are, by the methods' own description, oligonucleotide sequences and modifications (Table S1), which oligos assemble which substrate (Table S2), the number of trajectories inspected and replicates per figure (Table S3), and R-squared values for bi-exponential dwell-time fits (Table S4), plus MATLAB analysis code. No measurement table of any size is described as deposited.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. The data availability statement says the raw single-molecule videos are 'available on request' — the explicit Part A1 fail condition. No accession in any repository (GEO, SRA, Zenodo, Dryad, PRIDE, BioStudies) appears in the text, and the NCBI open-access package for PMC13494559 returns 404, so even the supplementary tables could not be retrieved programmatically. I verified the absence of accessions, not the presence of usable data.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL (assessed from the paper, since no file opened). The outcomes of interest — synapsis efficiency, dwell times, FRET (fluorescence resonance energy transfer, a molecular-ruler readout) state occupancies, AID (activation-induced deaminase) copy number per spot — exist only as plotted bar heights and fitted parameters in figures. Reconstructing them as a column would mean re-analysing single-molecule videos that are not distributed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Partial pass on the paper's description only: Supplementary Table S1 reportedly lists the actual oligonucleotide sequences and fluorophore modifications, and the AID mutants are named by substitution (K22E/R24S/R25E, R50E/K52E, R171E, R171E/R174E, and a seven-site combination), so sequence inputs would not need lookups. Not verified in a file.

a4_units_stated.note: The methods define each quantity with its unit or normalisation — synapsis efficiency as a ratio of colocalisation to substrate counts, dwell times in seconds, FRET efficiency as a 0-1 ratio, protein added in picomoles. Units are clear in the text; no units column was inspected.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The unit of analysis is a (substrate, protein variant) condition: roughly six to eight DNA structures (single-stranded, double-stranded, bubble, R-loop, D-loop, tailed D-loop) crossed with about eight protein variants, i.e. on the order of 50-100 aggregate measurements, far under the ~1,500-row bar and under the ~400 classification bar. Individual trajectories are more numerous but live only in the undistributed videos. No row count was verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: < 10 MB of supplementary tables; raw videos (hundreds of 500-frame movies) would be tens to hundreds of GB but are not available
a6_fits_laptop.note: The distributed material is trivially small. Pass is moot given A1 and A5.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download to compare against the paper, so the key verification this checklist exists to perform is impossible here.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle — every readout traces to a physical fluorescence measurement on a TIRF (total internal reflection fluorescence) microscope, not to another model's output. The concern is the manual step: trajectories were 'visually checked' and synapsis events 'manually truncated', so labels carry human-curation subjectivity.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable: with no distributed measurement table, any model here would be fitted to numbers read off published figures for a few dozen experimental conditions.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA structure and protein mutations to predict how often an antibody-diversifying enzyme glues two DNA pieces together.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered: one row per (DNA substrate shape, AID protein variant) pair, with the DNA sequence and the mutated residues as features. Roughly 50-100 such pairs exist, a count I could not verify because nothing is downloadable.
plain_idea.predict: Synapsis efficiency — the fraction of surface-tethered DNA molecules that capture a second DNA molecule — measured by counting colocalised fluorescent spots under a single-molecule microscope, plus how long each pairing lasts.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs studying class switch recombination (how B cells swap antibody types) and the chromosome translocations it can cause would want to know which DNA shapes and which parts of AID drive pairing; but with dozens of conditions this is a question for more experiments, not for a model.

ml_idea: None viable. The nearest idea — predicting protein-mediated DNA synapsis efficiency from substrate architecture and AID mutation — would need hundreds of measured conditions. A real version of this project would require a dedicated high-throughput single-molecule screen, which no public resource currently provides for AID.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset to size. The only distributed files are small supplementary tables of oligonucleotide sequences, replicate counts and curve-fit statistics.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement — 'raw single-molecule videos are available on request' kills it in one line, before any download is attempted.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A1 (raw single-molecule videos only on request; no repository accession anywhere in the text and no NCBI open-access package), A5 (the unit of analysis is a DNA-substrate-by-AID-mutant condition, of which there are tens, not thousands), A2 (the outcomes exist as figure bars and fitted parameters, not as a column) and A7 (no download exists to check counts against). This is a mechanistic biophysics paper whose contribution is a model of a molecular mechanism, not a measurement table; its supplementary material is oligonucleotide sequences, trajectory tallies and MATLAB analysis code.
